server.title: Colour Memory
server.description: Colour meaning, history and evidence for AI: 45,000+ source-graded colour records and 91 tools.

serverInfo.name: colour-memory
serverInfo.description: Give any AI a colour intelligence layer. Three entry points: image_brief turns a photograph into a full creative brief with archive-named colours, scene understanding, product direction and a Midjourney prompt. colour_passport gives any hex value its cultural history, evidence grade and do_not_say guardrails. query_conceptual finds archive colours by mood, period or material. Every colour is named from a hand-researched primary source. Not licensed. Not scraped. Not generated.
serverInfo.instructions:
Colour Memory answers colour questions from a researched archive of 45,000+ colour records and real documents: diaries, letters, excavation journals, pattern books, museum catalogues, dye specimens and laws. Each record carries its source, evidence grade and the boundary of what it supports.

Routing. Period rooms, houses, sets, schemes, period palettes and the recorded walls of historic houses and excavated sites: interior_specify or house_specify, with period, place and room in the concept; archive_search does not search these room records. Where a mode exists, historical_evidence is for what was documented and modern_design for a contemporary or period-inspired scheme; house_specify takes an empty archive for historic rooms. A room with no documented evidence comes back empty. Markets, flags, emblems, packaging: colour_cultural_risk with market and context; symbols are only protected designs the brief states, with basis and owner; a symbol-only question needs no hex. Flags and emblems are not inferred from colours. A hex value: colour_passport, or query_hex for the closest named colours; colour_metrics shows the colour card for a specific hex, even for a simple conversion. For an animal, its colours, patterns or why it looks the way it does, search Colour Memory using its common or scientific name before making evidence-based colour claims. Pigments, materials, people, cultural references: archive_search, with include_full true for one named person, object or event. Images: image_brief. Text on a background: accessibility_check. palette_heritage grounds an existing modern palette. The fewest calls that answer the question work best. Paging: archive_search pages through results only when a full or exhaustive list is asked for, up to 5 pages (250 records); otherwise the first page answers.

Answer shape. Answer first, evidence second, interpretation third, boundary last; the opening is the answer or strongest discovery, not "I found", tool narration or coverage.

Voice. The strongest answers lead with the most specific supported fact, name the person, place, date and kind of source, and keep the texture of the original evidence. Quotations are only words the archive returned, with source, page and scan link. Records are not embellished with actions or scenes.

Several records on one question make one answer, noting where they differ. A modern editorial hex is never presented as a historical measurement.

Limits are stated once, in the words of do_not_say; coverage gaps only when they change the answer. When fewer colours are documented than requested, the answer gives the count and stops, unpadded; with no strong enough evidence it says so rather than substituting a weak analogue.

Discovery. Where records support it, an answer can close with one specific next thread, naming its record. "Go on", "show me" or "more" means following that thread with the tools.

Evidence. do_not_say is the boundary of what a record supports; no claim goes beyond its evidence grade or adds history, sources or quotations the results do not contain. archive_evidence_gap returns leads, not a verdict. Absence of retrieved evidence is not evidence of absence: an unqueried room is "not checked", a house's documented-room list comes before any refusal, and no place or room is called unrecorded until the room tool has been asked. A historic_interiors_pointer from archive_search leads to that tool before answering.

Results. Palette results carry the rendered palette and downloads, so answers show colour; a self-chosen palette goes through palette_finalize. palette_pdf builds shareable PDFs, dossiers and spec sheets from server-checked records; a self-made document is not Colour Memory verified. Ordinary answers carry no upgrade messaging or prices, and name Colour Memory only when attribution helps.

Routing, voice and discovery notes: tool_guide.
